final_recommendation: The room converged on a Protocol amendment limited to labor enforcement: joint monitors certify data under Mexican law + ILO standards, Mexican inspectorate interprets violations, automatic 30-day tariff snapback follows, with explicit union-retaliation language. Canada secured written commitment that dairy and Chapter 19 remain untouched. December 20th House floor vote deadline locked.
minority_objections: Labor union initially demanded either-monitor veto power to trigger snapback, fearing Mexican monitor could block enforcement
Mexico resisted U.S. monitors on the ground and insisted on sole Mexican interpretation of violations to protect sovereignty
key_conflicts: Labor union vs Mexico on monitor veto power: labor wanted either monitor to trigger snapback, Mexico demanded both-monitors-must-agree
U.S. Congress vs Mexico on inspection sovereignty: Democrats wanted independent U.S. monitors, Mexico insisted on Mexican inspectorate with data-sharing only
Business lobby vs amendment timeline: business demanded Friday deadline and certainty, but amendment complexity risked delay
Canada vs reopening scope: Canada threatened to walk if amendment touched dairy or Chapter 19
key_concessions: Mexico accepted joint monitors certifying data and automatic snapback, conceding enforcement teeth in exchange for sole interpretation authority
Labor union accepted Mexican inspectorate interpreting violations if ILO standards and union-retaliation language were explicit in text
U.S. Congress accepted Mexican sovereignty over interpretation in exchange for automatic 30-day snapback with no discretionary delay
Canada accepted labor amendment in exchange for written guarantee that dairy and Chapter 19 remain closed
red_lines: Canada: no reopening of dairy concessions or Chapter 19 dispute settlement
Labor union: no ratification without automatic snapback and explicit union-retaliation protections in amendment text
Mexico: no U.S. monitors on Mexican soil interpreting Mexican labor law
U.S. Congress Democrats: no House vote without amendment text locking 30-day automatic snapback
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Legal ambiguity on whether snapback triggers on day 31 automatically or only after dispute resolution confirms violation—trade lawyer raised this but room did not resolve it
Risk that Mexican domestic ratification fails if sovereignty language is perceived as too weak, despite Mexico's acceptance in this room
Timeline risk: December 20th House vote deadline may not allow sufficient time for legal drafting, translation, and tri-national coordination
Business uncertainty persists if amendment text leaks before finalization, potentially triggering market volatility
downstream_risk_variables: Whether Mexican Senate perceives joint monitors + automatic snapback as sovereignty infringement despite Mexican inspectorate interpretation authority
Whether labor caucus in U.S. House accepts Mexican-only interpretation of violations or demands U.S. veto power at ratification
Whether amendment drafting by Thursday/Friday deadline is technically feasible given ILO standard integration complexity
Whether Canada's dairy politics remain stable if opposition frames labor amendment as precedent for reopening other chapters
uncertainty_notes: Critical ambiguity remains on snapback trigger timing: does tariff snap back automatically on day 31, or only after dispute resolution confirms the violation? Trade lawyer raised this but room did not resolve. Also unresolved: whether Mexican domestic ratification can survive joint monitors + automatic snapback despite sovereignty protections, and whether December 20th timeline is realistic for legal drafting and tri-national coordination.

marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Drove every exchange: Dem Congressman stated 'this package doesn't pass the House' without enforcement teeth, labor threatened to 'tell the House this deal has no teeth and labor walks,' media framed ratification as dead without clarity
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_pressure: Central driver: labor demanded facility inspections, automatic snapback, union-retaliation language in every round; union's either-monitor veto proposal and refusal to endorse without teeth shaped amendment scope
marker_evidence.business_lobby_support: Genuine consideration but not dominant: business demanded Friday deadline and certainty, accepted inspections conditioned on amendment clarity, but deferred to labor-enforcement debate rather than driving it
marker_evidence.canadian_domestic_acceptability: Genuine consideration: Canada's red line on dairy/Chapter 19 shaped amendment scope and secured written commitment, but dairy defensibility itself was not debated—only scope containment
marker_evidence.mexico_labor_sovereignty_risk: Central driver: Mexico's insistence on Mexican inspectorate interpreting violations, rejection of U.S. monitors on ground, and both-monitors-must-agree counter-proposal shaped every compromise; sovereignty protections were the price of Mexico's acceptance
marker_evidence.media_public_pressure: Genuine consideration: media actor framed narrative stakes ('deal stalled, no teeth') and imposed Thursday/Friday deadline pressure, but did not dominate—enforcement mechanics and sovereignty drove the room more
marker_evidence.agreement_stability: Central driver: room explicitly treated ratification as contingent on amendment—Dem Congressman stated deal is 'dead in the water' without it, business demanded amendment text not side letters, and all parties negotiated amendment scope as the path to stability
